title: Botox, Fillers & Med Spas: Safety and Free Assessments
description: Botox and dermal fillers explained: who can inject in the US, how to choose a safe med spa, risks to know, and what a free aesthetic assessment includes.
intro: Injectables are among the most popular aesthetic treatments in the US. Here is how to choose a qualified injector and a safe med spa.

image.alt: Woman receiving a facial treatment from a clinician

sections.html: Botulinum toxin products (Botox and others) relax specific muscles to soften expression lines, with results that typically wear off over a few months. Dermal fillers (often hyaluronic acid) add volume to areas such as the lips, cheeks and under-eyes. Both are prescription medical treatments, not beauty products.

• Rules on who may inject, and the level of physician supervision, vary by state.
  • Ask who the supervising physician is and who will perform your treatment.
  • Ask to see the product packaging: the FDA has warned about counterfeit and unapproved botulinum toxin.
  • Ask how complications such as vascular occlusion from fillers are handled.

More in our med spa safety guide.

Many med spas offer a free assessment and treatment plan. Pricing can be per unit (toxins) or per syringe (fillers), so ask for a total estimate. Cosmetic injectables are not covered by insurance; Botox for medical uses such as chronic migraine may be.

faqs.a: FDA-approved botulinum toxin products given by trained, licensed professionals have a well-established safety record for approved uses. Risks increase with unlicensed injectors or counterfeit products.
